slides.title:
A calibration choice,
not a release
slides.subtitle:
Which correction deserves another test?
Invented synthetic instrument responses; nonclinical.
slides.notes: All instrument signals, repeat counts, candidate formulas and screening limits are invented. The arbitrary unit AU is internal to this simulation. No physical instrument, certified standard or measured calibration is represented.

slides.title: The toy response bends at high input
slides.subtitle: Synthetic response = offset + gain + curvature + noise
slides.caption: SYN-C. AU = arbitrary simulation units.
slides.interpretation: A constant offset cannot remove input-dependent error.
slides.notes: The dashed identity line is a mathematical reference, not an empirical standard. Training uses six levels with four synthetic repeats each. This primary-rail contains one dominant figure and a complete native readout; no small secondary thumbnail is required.

flow_steps.title: Hold out
flow_steps.detail: 30 new values at ten interleaved levels.

slides.caption: SYN-C. Native editable stages; random seed 1401.
slides.notes: Offset correction subtracts the mean training response-minus-input. Affine and quadratic candidates fit input as a function of training response with least squares. Holdout values are generated independently using the same invented response law. No holdout tuning, extrapolation or real instrument calibration is performed.

slides.title: Rank corrections on one denominator
slides.subtitle: Synthetic holdout RMSE in AU; lower is better; n = 30 each
slides.caption: SYN-C. RMSE = sqrt(mean(residual squared)); bars start at zero. No significance claim.
slides.notes: The generator computes this native chart directly from the retained residual arrays. The illustrative RMSE screen is <=1.5 AU and the maximum-absolute-error screen is <=3 AU; neither is a real instrument specification. Actual pass counts and maxima are in the data ledger.

slides.title: Passing the screen earns another test
slides.subtitle: Invented decision rules; not a validated calibration specification

rows: New law, new seed, new noise
table.caption: SYN-C. All thresholds are invented for this nonclinical illustration.

slides.notes: The table expresses an authored decision policy. It is not a report of field failures or a confidence statement. Source-level validation verifies the same-denominator scores and checks whether the quadratic candidate actually clears both toy limits.

slides.title: Noise widens the residuals
slides.subtitle: Synthetic sensitivity rerun: same holdout design at three noise settings

figures.label: A
figures.title: Quadratic error under noise
figures.caption: One seeded synthetic split per noise setting.

slides.caption: SYN-C. Noise SD is 0.45, 0.90 or 1.80 AU.
slides.interpretation: A favorable toy fit does not certify robustness.
slides.notes: All three settings use the same generated standard-normal draws scaled by their noise SD, so the sweep changes one causal factor. Each setting refits all candidates on 24 training values and scores 30 holdout values. Only the quadratic residual distribution is plotted here; every candidate metric is retained in the JSON ledger. No Monte Carlo uncertainty interval is implied.

slides.title: Advance a candidate; withhold release
slides.subtitle: Illustrative selection under one invented response law
bullets: Take the quadratic inverse into a different synthetic response law.
Test drift, outliers and extrapolation before making a stronger claim.
Do not translate AU thresholds into physical instrument specifications.
slides.summary_callout: Synthetic screening only. No empirical calibration or deployment claim.
slides.notes: No real units, physical reference materials, instrument population, repeated run stability or uncertainty budget were modeled. The generator verifies that the recommendation is consistent with the toy metrics, not that this correction is suitable for any actual device.
